Campus Activewear.summary:
Three houses cover Campus, split between two bulls and one cautious hold. **Kotak** (Buy, ₹310) and **MO** (Buy, ₹330) are constructive, while **CLSA** (Hold, ₹247) sits 25–35% below the bull targets. Kotak upgraded to Buy from Add in May-2026 — an EPS-cut-with-upgrade, a valuation call rather than earnings momentum — on the back of a strong sneaker year (50% YoY growth) and sufficient price hikes to defend margins. CLSA's 4QFY26 update is the most granular: 12.3% revenue growth, gross margin down 26bps YoY but EBITDA margin up 51bps via operating leverage, and a 53bps miss vs their own estimate. MO's Buy ₹330 is unchanged from early-2025 and is the stalest of the three.

My own read: Campus is a credible mass-to-mid athletic brand in a market where Nike and Adidas are pricing out of reach for the bottom two-thirds of the population. The sneaker pivot is real — doubling sneaker sales in a year is a meaningful signal. But the brand moat remains thin; the logo refresh is a statement of aspiration, not yet of arrival. The bearish data point CLSA surfaces — gross margin declining even with volume recovery — is the right one to watch: premiumisation via sneakers works only if the product mix durably lifts gross margin, not just EBITDA where operating leverage can temporarily mask gross-margin pressure. Online growing at 18.9% vs distribution at 5.5% is also a structural concern: the online channel inflates topline optics but compresses margins relative to the trade. I'd sit closer to Kotak's ₹310 than MO's ₹330, with the upgrade credible only if the next two quarters confirm sneaker gross-margin accretion.

CLSA|260526.change: PT ₹247 unchanged; Hold maintained — no delta vs prior.
CLSA|260526.view:
CLSA is the disciplined sceptic. Their ₹247 target is 20–34% below the bull-camp numbers and implies the stock is roughly fairly valued post the 4QFY26 beat. The note surfaces the gross-margin miss (−53bps vs their estimate) that Kotak's more bullish framing glosses over. Their observation on online-channel dominance (18.9% growth vs 5.5% for distribution) is structurally important: it complicates the premiumisation narrative because online economics are thinner than offline trade margins.

This is a credible anchor for the range. If gross margins don't inflect upward with a richer sneaker mix, ₹247 is the gravitational pull — operating-leverage stories lose their charm the moment topline slows or the channel mix skews further online.

Kotak|260526.change: PT ₹310 unchanged; rating upgraded to Buy (from Add). EPS cut ~10% FY2027E and ~2% FY2028E alongside the upgrade.
Kotak|260526.view:
An EPS-cut upgrade is a valuation signal, not an earnings signal: Kotak is saying the stock derated enough during the year to make the risk/reward attractive even with trimmed estimates. The sneaker doubling is the thesis anchor — Kotak is betting premiumisation lifts the mix durably. The unchanged FV of ₹310 means the upgrade was entirely price-driven.

I find this credible but would watch FY2027 delivery closely. If the EPS cut proves optimistic again — a second consecutive downward revision — the Buy thesis softens fast. The brand-logo soft launch is a monitoring point: distribution-channel recovery (currently only +5.5%) is the proof that brand equity is broadening beyond the online channel, not just concentrating there.

MO|250529.change: Buy ₹330 maintained — unchanged from at least Feb-2025. Dated May-2025; no local PDF available to compare prevTP/prevCall directly.
MO|250529.view: MO's ₹330 is the most aggressive target and the most stale, written a full year before the Kotak and CLSA May-2026 updates. With Kotak cutting FY2027E EPS ~10% in the same results cycle, MO's unchanged target raises a question: has MO refreshed their model, or is this a re-release? Without the detailed note, I'd treat ₹330 as a stale upper bound rather than a well-grounded current view. The directional Buy is likely still defensible given the sneaker runway, but the magnitude of implied upside needs to be stress-tested against the revised estimates that peers are using.

Carborundum Universal.summary:
Three of four houses are bearish on CUMI; **Kotak** (Sell, FV ₹930), **PL** (Reduce, ₹986), and **ICICI** (Sell, ₹895) all see meaningful downside from CMP ₹1,102. The sole bull — **Sharekhan** (Buy, ₹1,100 from Mar-2025) — has had its target effectively met by the stock price and the call is 15 months stale. Kotak raised their FV from ₹785 to ₹930 on domestic recovery and loss-making subsidiary exits, yet kept Sell; PL downgraded to Reduce while raising TP from ₹835 to ₹986 — both implying the near-term improvement is real but the valuation is running ahead of fundamentals. The real debate is whether the exit of loss-making overseas subsidiaries and the new-age materials capex cycle creates a multi-year RoCE re-rating — or whether the stock, already above all sell-side targets, has priced that scenario in.

My own read: CUMI is a quality Murugappa franchise in a genuinely niche industrial segment where domestic competition is structurally limited to Saint-Gobain Abrasives and Grindwell Norton. That oligopoly moat is real and durable. But the Sell consensus is correct on valuation: at CMP ₹1,102, the stock is above every single sell-side target including the bull case. The risk the sell-side is partly underplaying is the capex commitment on non-oxide ceramics and advanced materials — long-gestation, capital-intensive bets where CUMI is punching above its weight globally, and where payback timelines have already slipped. If FY2027 capex payback disappoints, the recovery narrative unravels quickly. I'd watch two things above all: (1) the pace and structure of the Russia subsidiary exit — a messy unwind could land as a one-time earnings hit the market hasn't modelled; (2) domestic abrasives volume growth, which is the clean, high-ROCE core and the best leading signal of underlying business quality.

Kotak|260518.change: FV raised ₹785→₹930 (+18.5%); Sell maintained. CMP ₹1,102 implies ~15.6% downside to FV.
Kotak|260518.view:
Kotak is the freshest and most detailed bear. The FV raise is honest acknowledgement that domestic recovery and loss-making sub exits are real positives — ₹785 was arguably too punitive. But ₹930 at CMP ₹1,102 is a clear valuation call with ~15% implied downside even on an upgraded model. Their key monitorable — new-age business capex paying off in FY2027+ — is the correct variable: it's unproven, it's burning FCF, and it could swing RoCE materially either way.

I'd weight Kotak's caution heavily. Their sector view is 'Cautious' on Capital Goods broadly, so there's a macro overlay. But the CUMI-specific concern about unproven capex is independent of that sector call and stands on its own.

PL|260516.change: Downgraded to Reduce (from Hold); TP raised ₹835→₹986. Prior trajectory: Accumulate ₹1,601 (Nov-2024) → Hold ₹1,028 (May-2025) → Hold ₹835 (Aug-2025) → Reduce ₹986 (May-2026).
PL|260516.view: PL's downgrade-with-TP-raise is a telling combination: near-term numbers were mixed but improving (domestic rebound, subsidiary path clearing), yet PL cut the rating because the stock has run beyond what their model justifies. The prior trajectory — persistent TP cuts from ₹1,601 to ₹835 over 18 months — shows PL has been consistently right to be cautious on this name; they don't appear to be talking it down. The ₹986 Reduce at CMP ₹1,102 is the least aggressive bear target but still implies ~10.5% downside, and is directionally aligned with Kotak.

ICICI|250514.change: Sell ₹895; dated May-2025 — 13+ months old. Earlier ICICI call: Sell ₹1,450 (Aug-2024). No subsequent update in local library or trendlyne.
ICICI|250514.view: ICICI's Sell at ₹895 is the most aggressive on downside but also the most stale. Written referencing CUMI's 5-year plan to 'arrest the slide', it predates the domestic recovery narrative and the loss-making sub exit announcements that shaped Kotak's and PL's May-2026 updates. The 13-month gap with no refresh is notable — either ICICI has deprioritised the name or remains unmoved by the recovery data. At CMP ₹1,102, their ₹895 target implies ~18.8% downside. That's not obviously wrong — it's consistent with the Kotak/PL direction — but I'd treat it as stale context, not a current actionable call, until ICICI publishes a post-4QFY26 update.

Sharekhan|250319.change: Upgraded to Buy (from Hold ₹1,620 in Nov-2024); TP ₹1,100. Target has been met — CMP ₹1,102. No subsequent refresh.
Sharekhan|250319.view: Sharekhan's contrarian upgrade in Mar-2025 at ₹1,100 — when the rest of the street was cutting targets — looks well-timed in retrospect. The call played out. But with CMP at the target and no subsequent note, this is an exhausted bull call with no residual upside implied. Sharekhan would need to raise their target meaningfully to sustain the Buy thesis at current prices. Until a refresh appears, this is effectively a hold or exit signal, not a new entry point. The upgrade was a good trade; whether CUMI is still an investment at ₹1,100+ is a question Sharekhan hasn't yet answered.

Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail.summary:
Morgan Stanley stands apart as the lone bull (ADD, ₹127) — nearly double the ₹60–65 cluster shared by CLSA (Hold, ₹60), Kotak (Reduce, ₹65), and Motilal Oswal (Neutral, ₹65). The central debate is whether **Pantaloons**' operational recovery (19% revenue growth, 14% LTL in 4QFY26; 20–22 new stores guided for FY27) can outrun the structural cash burn (₹14.4 bn consumed in FY26, balance sheet flipping to net debt of ₹1.5 bn). CLSA and MO are effectively flat-on-the-stock neutrals; **Kotak** is the most cautious, having just cut PT ₹70→₹65 on cash-flow concerns. MO has trimmed its target steadily from ₹285 (pre-demerger) to ₹65 over 18 months. Morgan Stanley's ₹127 appears to price in a multi-year re-rating as the demerger-simplified entity (post-Madura spin-off) executes on Pantaloons + ethnic portfolio; the rest see too much cash drag for the valuation to be compelling now.

My own read: ABFRL post-demerger is a structurally different business — the Madura brands (Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly) were the earnings-quality anchor; what remains is the Pantaloons turnaround, a collection of early-stage ethnic labels (Jaypore, Tarun Tahiliani, Shantnu & Nikhil), and TMRW (the D2C aggregator), none of which are cash-generative yet. Pantaloons is showing real signs of life and management credibility is rebuilding, but ₹14.4 bn of cash consumption in a single year with EBITDA margins contracting 200 bps despite 16% revenue growth tells you the ethnic/TMRW investments are still a long way from self-funding. I'd watch two things: (1) **free cash flow** — the bear case wins outright if FCF stays deeply negative through FY27; (2) **ethnic LTL** (currently only 4%) — that is the long-duration bet underpinning Morgan Stanley's ₹127. Until ethnic inflects meaningfully or cash burn narrows, the honest range is the ₹60–65 cluster, not the bull target.

MorganStan|260602.view:
Morgan Stanley's ADD at ₹127 is a significant outlier — the next highest target is barely half. The note is a management-guided India Investment Forum takeaway, which adds self-selection risk: management naturally sounded confident on Pantaloons strategy, customer experience resets, and the 20–22 store rollout.

I'd discount this target meaningfully. A ₹127 fair value requires flawless concurrent execution across Pantaloons *and* ethnic/TMRW while FCF is still deeply negative — a scenario that looks 2–3 years optimistic given current margin trajectory. The directional bull case (demerger clarity, Pantaloons gaining traction) is not wrong, but the price bridge is aggressive. Useful as a best-case anchor; not a sufficient reason to own the stock today.

CLSA|260527.change: No prior TP recorded in PDF library; HOLD maintained at ₹60.
CLSA|260527.view:
CLSA's Hold at ₹60 is arguably the most intellectually cautious position — it acknowledges the 4QFY26 beat (EBITDA 11.5% above consensus) while correctly flagging that headline LTL of 14% shrank to 7% once the EOSS timing benefit is stripped. The ethnic portfolio LTL at 4% is a quiet warning that the second leg of the bull thesis is not yet working.

The ₹60 target sitting *below* Kotak's Reduce of ₹65 is oddly unambitious for a Hold — it implies near-zero upside from CMP, making the rating inconsistent unless CLSA is effectively waiting for a cleaner ethnic data point before deciding direction. Worth watching whether they step up or cut on FY27 Q1 results.

Kotak|260527.view:
Kotak is the most rigorous bear and, arguably, the most useful contrarian voice in this cluster. The ₹14.4 bn cash consumption in FY26 and the net-debt reversal are hard balance-sheet facts that bullish framing around Pantaloons LTL tends to paper over. EBITDA margins contracting 200 bps despite 16% revenue growth means scale is not automatically converting to profitability — the inter-segment accounting tailwind in the base quarter makes the reported margin look even worse in clean comparison.

I find this the most credible near-term call. The key stress-test is how long the ethnic/TMRW burn continues: if those segments keep consuming ₹8–10 bn/year while Pantaloons gradually recovers, the debt trajectory becomes the dominant risk factor, not the P&L. Kotak's Reduce at ₹65 is defensible unless management delivers a sharp FCF inflection in the next two quarters.

MO|260526.change: PT cut ₹75→₹65 (prior note 26 Feb 2026, PT ₹75); Neutral maintained.
MO|260526.view:
MO's Neutral with a TP cut from ₹75 to ₹65 is consistent with a pattern of steady downward revisions — from ₹285 pre-demerger to ₹65 now — as the demerger reshuffled the earnings base and cash burn persisted. The headline "Strong 4Q growth; cash outflow remains high" captures the bull/bear tension with unusual honesty for a sell-side note.

At ₹65 Neutral, MO is in near-identical territory to Kotak's Reduce; the only distinction is the rating label. Not a differentiated view, but a reasonable central-case anchor. The steady TP erosion over 18 months suggests the market has consistently surprised to the downside on FCF — watch whether MO joins Kotak at Reduce if FY27 H1 cash flow doesn't improve.

Bharat Electronics.summary:
Four houses are on BEL post FY26 results: **Jeff** (Buy, PT ₹585) and **CLSA** (Outperform, PT ₹522) are constructive; **Nomura** (Neutral, PT ₹454) sees fair value as already exceeded; **PL** (Hold, PT ₹374, Jul-2025) is deeply stale. Targets span ₹374–585 — a wide spread that mostly reflects vintage, not genuine analytical disagreement. The live debate is between Jeff/CLSA's view that the ₹550bn FY27 order flow guidance (85% YoY, anchored by ₹300bn QRSAM) re-rates the stock further, and Nomura's view that it is already priced in. Jeff raised PT ₹565→₹585 on the FY26 beat (EBITDA margin 29.2% vs 27%+ guidance; order inflow ₹297bn vs ₹270bn guidance). CLSA and Nomura held their TPs flat at ₹522 and ₹454 respectively. The post-India-Pakistan conflict order acceleration is the event that split consensus: Jeff/CLSA treat it as a durable pull-forward of multi-year spend; Nomura treats it as already reflected in the price.

My own read: BEL is a structurally better business than it was three years ago — the product mix has shifted from spares/maintenance toward complex systems (QRSAM, LRSAM, electronic fuses), which carries higher margins and stickier revenue. The ₹739bn order book with 81% executable in the next 12 months gives genuinely rare revenue visibility for a company of this scale. That said, BEL's growth is almost entirely hostage to defence capex budget allocation; any fiscal stress in the coalition or a durable India-Pakistan ceasefire could defer the very orders now being priced in. At current multiples, the bull case (Jeff ₹585) already embeds QRSAM landing on schedule and margins holding — leaving little room for execution slippage. I align closer to Nomura's valuation discipline: the franchise is real, but I'd rather buy the first sign of order-flow disappointment than chase the post-results pop. Key watchpoints: QRSAM order crystallisation by H1FY27 and whether FY27 execution tracks the ₹550bn guidance run-rate in Q1-Q2.

CLSA|260521.view:
CLSA's 'Delivered again' is a credible, well-titled note — BEL did deliver sector-leading 16% YoY revenue growth while beating margin consensus (29.2% vs 27%+). The US$12bn pipeline with US$6.3bn expected in the next 12 months is a compelling forward look, and CLSA grounds it in the Modi 3.0 accelerated-order thesis rather than hope.

The problem is that CLSA's TP at ₹522 is essentially pinned to the current post-results price, offering zero margin of safety. That makes the Outperform a 'hold at this level, we just can't bring ourselves to downgrade' call rather than a genuine Buy. I'd use CLSA as a useful check on the order-pipeline math (they've done the work) but treat the rating with scepticism — a flat TP revision is a soft signal of diminishing upside confidence.

Nomura|260521.view:
Nomura's 'trading ahead' framing is the most intellectually honest call in the pack. It is not disputing the fundamentals — the ₹739bn order book, the healthy FY27 guidance, the margin beat are all acknowledged — it is simply saying the market has fully discounted them and then some.

This is the most useful counterweight for a portfolio holder with a large position: Nomura is effectively saying 'the stock needs QRSAM to crystallise and margins to hold just to justify the current price.' If either slips a quarter, the de-rating from elevated multiples could be sharp. I find this the most usable note of the four — not because I'm bearish on BEL's franchise, but because valuation discipline matters when the order-flow catalyst is widely anticipated. Nomura's ₹454 target implies meaningful downside from current prices; I would not dismiss it.

Jeff|260520.view:
Jeff is the most bullish and has the highest target, grounded in delivered results rather than hope. The FY26 order inflow beat (₹297bn vs ₹270bn guidance) plus the ₹550bn FY27 guidance — 85% YoY — give Jeff confidence to nudge the PT higher, and the margin beat (29.2% EBITDA) removes a key bear concern.

The analysis is rigorous, but at ₹585 the stock needs QRSAM orders to land on schedule and margins to sustain at 29%+ — a compounding of optimistic assumptions. I give Jeff credit for the underlying work but would apply a ~10% execution-risk haircut to the target. The note is worth reading closely for the order-book composition detail (LRSAM, LCA, electronic fuses, BMP-II) — that breakdown is the best publicly available visibility map for BEL's revenue pipeline.

PL|250730.view: This note is now ~11 months old and is not actionable. The India-Pakistan conflict order acceleration, the FY26 results beat, and the ₹550bn FY27 guidance were all subsequent events that PL has not yet reflected in a published update in the library. The ₹374 Hold is deeply stale — BEL's price has likely moved well above that level. Treat this as historical context only; do not weight it in any current view.
